findings.title: Referer-based host check is weak and bypassable; X-Frame-Options set to ALLOWALL
findings.body: Embedding access control relies entirely on the Referer header's host equalling SiteSetting.embeddable_host. The Referer is attacker-controlled outside browsers and may be stripped or spoofed. Once it passes, X-Frame-Options is set to ALLOWALL, so any page that can forge or strip the referer can frame the content. A proper fix would use CSP frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options ALLOW-FROM with the configured host instead of ALLOWALL.

findings.title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript string
findings.body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` is placed inside a JS string. ERB HTML-escapes it, but that does not protect a JS string context in all cases, and the referer is user-controlled. It is also the full referer URL, not an origin, so postMessage's targetOrigin may not match (postMessage requires an origin, and a full URL with a path is reduced or rejected in some browsers). Use `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` with a scheme, or `j`/to_json escaping.

findings.title: Weak origin check uses indexOf on discourseUrl
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check, not an equality check. An origin such as `http://a` or an empty/short string that is a substring of discourseUrl would pass. Compare origins for equality instead.

findings.title: Unescaped URL and imported HTML are stored and rendered raw (stored XSS)
findings.body: Remote HTML (from feed or readability) is stored as raw and served unsanitized via cook_method raw_html and `raw post.cooked`; the feed-supplied URL is interpolated into an `<a href='...'>` without escaping. Feed or page content containing script or attribute injection is therefore served from the forum origin and embedded in the iframe. The content should be sanitized, and the URL escaped.

findings.title: import mutates the caller's contents string with <<
findings.body: `contents << ...` mutates the argument in place. If the string is frozen it raises, and callers' strings are altered. It also means the sha1 includes the footer, so it will be recomputed identically only if the footer is the same. Use a new string instead.

findings.title: Kernel#open on user-influenced URL (SSRF / command execution)
findings.body: `open(url)` with open-uri's Kernel#open will run a shell command if the string begins with `|`, and fetches arbitrary URLs. `import_remote` is reachable from the retrieve_topic job with the user-supplied embed_url. The host is checked against embeddable_host, but disqus.thor passes arbitrary links. In PollFeed, `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has the same problem. Use `URI.parse(url).open` or Net::HTTP with scheme validation.

findings.title: Race creating duplicate embeds; transaction doesn't prevent duplicate topics
findings.body: The check `embed.blank?` followed by creating the post and TopicEmbed is racy. Concurrent jobs for the same URL create two topics, then TopicEmbed.create! hits the unique index and raises. The raise happens after PostCreator has committed side effects (the rollback is inside the transaction, but job enqueues occur in PostCreator, and the post was created). Handle RecordNotUnique or use a lock.

findings.title: absolutize_urls drops/mishandles ports and protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: `prefix << ...` mutates an interpolated string (fine) but the port rule omits the port for 80 or 443 regardless of scheme, so an http URL on 443 or an https URL on 80 is wrong. Also, `//host/path` protocol-relative hrefs start with '/' and are rewritten into `prefix/host/path`, which is broken.

findings.title: Feed item content may be nil / String#scrub on Ruby <2.1, no error handling
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError if an item has no content (e.g. only description), aborting the whole poll. `String#scrub` is also unavailable before Ruby 2.1, which this Rails 4.0-era app likely runs on. Any one bad item stops the import of the rest, and sidekiq retry is disabled. The `feed_key` method is unused.

findings.title: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever.new to be called, but controller enqueues a job
findings.body: The controller enqueues Jobs :retrieve_topic, whereas the spec 'tells the topic retriever to work' expects TopicRetriever.new and retrieve to be invoked directly. This only passes if jobs run inline in test, and the expectation is brittle. Additionally, the `loading` render followed by `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` caches the loading page. Also an unauthenticated visitor can enqueue a job for an arbitrary embed_url; the throttle only runs later in the job.

findings.title: Invalid ERB `<%- end if %>` breaks template
findings.body: Line 6 is `<%- end if %>`, which is a syntax error (`end if` with no condition). The template will fail to compile, so the embed best page always errors. It should be `<%- end %>`. Also, when `@topic_view` posts is empty, the view still links via topic.url.

findings.title: skip_validations added silently to revise! affects all callers
findings.body: The new `skip_validations` option makes `@post.save` bypass validations. It is undocumented, and a blank line was removed in revise!. It is only used by TopicEmbed, but the option is exposed to every caller of the revisor. Fine if intentional, but it should be documented and tested.

findings.title: Non-atomic setnx + expire throttle
findings.body: `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is non-atomic. If the process dies between the two, the key never expires and the URL is permanently throttled. Use `set` with `nx` and `ex` options or `setex`-style atomic operations.

findings.title: Unrelated edit to an existing migration adds force: true (drops table)
findings.body: Modifying an already-existing migration to `force: true` makes `create_table` drop an existing top_topics table if the migration is re-run. The change is unrelated to this feature and is data-destructive. The whitespace change to migrate_word_counts is also unrelated noise.

findings.title: Weak tests: 'is 404' only asserts not success; missing coverage for view/XSS/URL edge cases
findings.body: The first test is named '404' but only asserts `should_not be_success`, and it would pass for the wrong reason (the referer check fails before params.require runs). No tests cover referer host mismatch, invalid-URI referers, rendering best.html.erb (which would have caught the template syntax error), or PollFeed.poll_feed itself.
